text: Bithumb Asset injects $75 million into Vietnamese ultra-luxury-resort, targeting 2029 launch

Bithumb Asset is doubling down on its Southeast Asian real estate portfolio, injecting over KRW100 billion ($75 million) from its own internal reserves to redevelop a 5-star resort in Hoi An, central Vietnam.
The move underscores the company's strong financial commitment to the project and is expected to significantly accelerate construction.
It recently announced a KRW112 billion ($84.4 million) capital increase for Asia Estate, its wholly-owned subsidiary that acts as the central hub for its international real estate ventures.

Representing 17.2 per cent of Bithumb Asset's total assets, which stood at KRW651.4 billion ($486 million) as of the end of the second quarter of 2026, the massive capital injection marks the company's first investment exceeding $75 million since spinning off from its parent company.
Bypassing High Interest Rates with Internal Funding
Following the capital increase, Asia Estate rapidly deployed the funds to Goldburger Co., Ltd. - the local entity executing the Vietnam project.
The deployment consisted of a KRW66.9 billion ($50 million) direct equity investment and a KRW40.1 billion ($30 million) short-term loan.
Notably, the entire sum was financed internally.
Industry analysts view Bithumb Asset's reliance on its own balance sheet as a highly strategic move.
By bypassing local credit markets in a high-interest rate environment, the company mitigates heavy borrowing costs and optimizes cash flow for its flagship overseas project.
To fund the deal, the parent company strategically restructured its asset portfolio.

While Bithumb Asset's cash reserves hovered at just KRW41 billion ($30.6 million) at the end of the second quarter, it held KRW286.7 billion ($214 million) in short-term trading securities, primarily US Treasuries.
Liquidating a portion of this portfolio provided the deep liquidity needed to fast-track the Vietnam venture.
An Ultra-Luxury "Conrad by Hilton" landmark
The destination for this capital is a prime beachfront property at Cua Dai Beach in Hoi An, formerly known as the Golden Sand Resort.
Under the management of Goldburger (established in 2019), the site is undergoing a sweeping transformation into an ultra-luxury complex originally developed under the name SUNYATA Hoi An .
Elevating the project's global profile, the developer has inked a management agreement with Hilton's top-tier luxury brand, Conrad.
Upon completion, the property will officially debut as Conrad Hoi An , positioning itself as a premier destination in central Vietnam's booming tourism hub.
Spearheading Asia Estate's overseas real estate ventures is CEO Mr. Cha Kyung-ho (Milo Cha), who boasts a unique and impressive professional background.

A graduate of South Korea's Bucheon High School and the University of Seoul (Class of 2002, Taxation), Mr. Cha made a strategic pivot from his role as a researcher at Samjong KPMG into the construction sector.

Joining industry giant Hyundai E&C in 2011, he built his expertise within the Real Estate Investment & Development team, rising to a managerial position before departing in 2018 to join Bithumb's Strategic Planning and Investment division.

During his tenure at Hyundai E&C, leveraging his military background with KATUSA (Korean Augmentation To the United States Army), Mr. Cha participated in the domestic relocation project of the US 8th Army base.
He also gained extensive hands-on experience managing international projects across Indonesia, Singapore, and Vietnam - most notably the Song Gia Resort expansion.
This rigorous background equipped him with deep analytical insights into the Southeast Asian real estate market and a robust local network.
Building on this foundation, Mr. Cha has been deeply embedded in the Vietnamese market since joining Bithumb.
Relocating to Da Nang around 2019, the seasoned executive has been instrumental in securing local partnerships, acquiring prime land, and navigating complex commercial deals.

Furthermore, after successfully passing the US CPA exam in early 2025, Mr. Cha has fully leveraged his academic background in taxation to concurrently oversee the firm's fund management operations through bond and equity investments in Vietnam.
His appointment as CEO of Asia Estate early last year was a clear signal of Bithumb Asset's intent to focus its full weight on the Vietnam mega-project.

Now, backed by a formidable KRW112 billion ($84.4 billion) war chest, Mr. Cha is fully empowered to push the Conrad Hoi An development into high gear, keeping the project firmly on track for its anticipated 2029 grand opening under the guidance of this proven leader.
